papers.title: Fast Microwave-free State Preparation and Measurement of Superconducting Qubits
papers.abstract: Fast, high-fidelity, scalable state preparation and measurement is critical to the realization of a quantum computing system. The state-of-the-art methods for preparation and readout of superconducting qubits require finely tuned microwave signals and ~100 ns of measurement time, which are major obstacles to the scalability and performance of superconducting quantum computers. Here, we have demonstrated novel, microwave-free methods for both preparation and readout of superconducting qubits with >99% fidelity in only 10 ns for either operation while maintaining qubit coherence. This technology is compatible with scalable superconducting digital control systems, and using quantum flux parametrons for amplification, we demonstrated full quantum-to-digital conversion in only 15 ns, which is an order of magnitude faster than state-of-the-art microwave-based techniques.

summary.summary: Fast microwave-free state preparation and measurement of superconducting qubits is demonstrated using strong coupling between a high-coherence computational qubit (CQ) and a flux qubit (FQ), achieving >99% fidelity in 10 ns for each operation. Combined with quantum flux parametron amplification and an analog-to-digital converter, full quantum-to-digital conversion is completed in 15 ns—an order of magnitude faster than dispersive readout—while remaining compatible with scalable superconducting digital control systems.
summary.motivation: Dispersive cQED readout requires ~100 ns and quantum-limited amplifiers with low saturation power, both major scalability obstacles. Moreover, superconducting SFQ-based digital control systems require microwave delivery to the millikelvin stage, which is incompatible with near-term scaling.
summary.method: The CQ photonic state is adiabatically swapped into the FQ via a large (~1–2 GHz) engineered anticrossing, then the FQ is annealed with a linear flux ramp that projects the photonic state into a persistent circulating current (~100 nA). State preparation uses rapid adiabatic passage: a $\Delta$ flux pulse creates an excitation in the FQ that is swapped back into the CQ. Superposition states are prepared by annealing at the degeneracy point ($\Delta = 0$).
summary.result: Over 282 devices from six fabrication lots, preparation and readout fidelities approach 99% (maximum 99.7%) with optimal timing of 10 ns each. Two stages of QFPs amplify the FQ current to digital levels in <2.5 ns per stage with error ~$10^{-5}$, enabling complete quantum-to-digital conversion in 15 ns. The $T_1$ measured is 50 µs and $T_2^* = 24.0(6)$ µs for the CQ.
